questions.stem: By what other name is the galaxy schema known?
questions.explanation: The galaxy schema is also known as the fact constellation schema.

questions.stem: How does the galaxy schema compare in complexity with the star and snowflake schemas?
options: It is simpler than star but more complex than snowflake
It is more complex than both
It has no dimensions, so complexity does not apply
questions.explanation: The galaxy schema is more complex than the star and snowflake schemas.

questions.stem: How many fact tables does a galaxy schema contain?
questions.explanation: A galaxy schema divides the star schema into smaller star schemas where there is more than one fact table.

questions.stem: What are the dimensions that connect multiple fact tables across multiple star schemas called?
questions.explanation: Dimensions which can connect with multiple fact tables across multiple star schemas are known as conformed dimensions.

questions.stem: What structural change does a galaxy schema make to a star schema?
options: It merges all dimensions into the fact table
It divides the star schema into smaller star schemas with reusable dimensions connecting them
It normalises the fact table into 3NF
questions.explanation: The galaxy schema further divides the star schema into small star schemas, with more than one fact table and reusable dimensions connecting them.

questions.stem: Which schema answers the question of where conformed dimensions appear in dimensional modelling?
questions.explanation: Star and snowflake schemas describe facts and dimensions, but it is the galaxy schema where conformed dimensions come into play.

questions.stem: What is a reusable dimension in a galaxy schema?
options: A dimension copied separately for each fact table
A dimension that connects multiple fact tables
A dimension stored in the OLTP system
A dimension that has been deleted and restored
A dimension with only one row
questions.explanation: A reusable dimension connects multiple fact tables; such dimensions are known as conformed dimensions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of the galaxy schema?
options: It is also called the fact constellation schema
It contains more than one fact table
It has exactly one fact table at its centre
It is more complex than the star schema
questions.explanation: A galaxy schema has more than one fact table; a single central fact table describes the star schema.

questions.stem: The galaxy schema belongs to which data warehousing approach?
questions.explanation: Star, snowflake and galaxy schemas all belong to Ralph Kimball's dimensional data warehousing approach.

questions.stem: What do the small star schemas within a galaxy schema share?
options: Conformed dimensions that connect their fact tables
questions.explanation: The small star schemas share reusable, conformed dimensions that connect their multiple fact tables.
